explanation: It is also called glutinous rice, yet it contains no gluten. Its stickiness comes from a starch that is almost all amylopectin.

claims.text: Mochi is made by pounding cooked glutinous (sticky) rice into a smooth, elastic dough.
Mochi is not made by pounding wheat flour, red beans or taro.
Glutinous rice contains no gluten; it is sticky because its starch is almost entirely amylopectin.
